Default priors of the EFSA Bayesian benchmark dose modelling

Source: R/efsa.R
efsapriors.Rd

The default (weakly informative) priors of the Bayesian benchmark dose modelling of EFSA (2022), as in its R package BMABMDR (Kremer et al. 2026), for a model in the BMD parameterisation of drmTMB (bmdpar): PERT priors for the response at dose zero (background), the response at high doses (maximum response) and the BMD, lognormal priors for the steepness and for the residual standard deviation. The result gives the arguments of drmTMB; bmdefsa fits a set of models with these priors and averages them.

Usage

efsapriors(
  form,
  data,
  model,
  family = c("gaussian", "lognormal", "binomial"),
  bmr = NULL,
  def = NULL,
  background = NULL,
  maxresponse = NULL,
  bmd = NULL,
  dprior = c("default", "alternative"),
  extended = TRUE
)

# S3 method for class 'efsapriors'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

form

formula of the response and the dose, as in drmTMB

data

a data.frame

model

one of "weibull2", "weibull1", "loglogistic", "lognormal", "gamma", "multistage", and for the binomial family "probit" and "logit"

family

"gaussian", "lognormal" or "binomial"

bmr, def

the benchmark response and its definition (see bmd); by default bmr=0.05 with def="relative" for gaussian and lognormal, and bmr=0.1 with def="excess" for binomial, the defaults of EFSA (2022)

background, maxresponse, bmd

informative priors: c(min, mode, max) or a prior (see priors); NULL for the defaults; maxresponse only for continuous responses

dprior

"default" or "alternative" prior of the steepness

extended

logical, the upper bound of the default BMD prior is three times the highest dose (TRUE) or the highest dose

x

an efsapriors object

...

not used

Value

an efsapriors object, a list with the EFSA model (name), the arguments model, family, curvelink, start, fix, prior and bmdpar of drmTMB, the direction of the curve (increasing) and whether it levels off (flat)

Details

The models are those of EFSA (2022) available in drcTMB: weibull2 (exponential), weibull1 (inverse exponential), loglogistic (Hill), lognormal (log-normal), gamma, and multistage of degree 2 (quadratic exponential, LMS two-stage), and for quantal responses also probit and logit (the probit and logistic models of EFSA, pnorm(b1 + b4 x^b3) and plogis(b1 + b4 x^b3): the power model with curvelink="probit" or "logit"). Families: "gaussian" (normal distribution), "lognormal" (fitted with curvelink="log": the curve is the log of the median, as the lognormal models of EFSA) and "binomial" (quantal responses, with b2 fixed at 1).

Default priors, with the response means at dose zero (y0) and at the highest dose (yN) (geometric means for lognormal), the benchmark response q and the highest dose dN:

  • background, increasing curve: pert(0.001, y0, 2 y0); decreasing: pert(0.5 y0, y0, 2 y0); quantal: pert(max(L/2, 1/(10 n0)), max(p0, 1/(5 n0)), min(3 U/2, 1 - 1/(10 n0))) with the observed proportion p0 of the n0 controls and its confidence interval (L, U) of prop.test (lower bound 1e-8 without events in the controls); shape 4. For the probit and logit models the prior is on the background probability pnorm(b1) or plogis(b1).

  • maximum response (continuous): increasing pert(y0 (1.01 + q), yN, 2 yN), or pert(y0 (1.01 + q), 3 yN, 6 yN) if the curve does not level off at the high doses; decreasing pert(0.5 yN, yN, y0 (1 - q - 0.01)), or pert(0.1 yN, 0.5 yN, y0 (1 - q - 0.01)); shape 4. Whether the curve levels off follows from a fractional polynomial of degree 2 of the means: its last slope on the log-dose scale is below half its largest slope. EFSA puts this prior on the fold change, the maximum response divided by the mode of the background; here it is on the maximum response (the asymptote) itself.

  • BMD: pert(0, dN/2, 3 dN) (extended=TRUE) or pert(0, dN/2, dN), with shape 0.0001, nearly uniform.

  • steepness d: |b3| lognormal(1, 1) (EFSA truncates log d at 5, which removes a probability of 3e-5 and is left out) or, with dprior="alternative", lognormal(0.4, sqrt(0.5)), for a sensitivity analysis (the power b3 of the probit and logit models has the same prior); for decreasing curves of the log-dose models b3 is negative, with the prior negate(lognormal(...)). The multistage model of degree 2 in the BMD parameterisation is the quadratic exponential model of EFSA, with the technical parameter log_d (in place of b3), with the prior normal(0, 1) of EFSA.

  • residual standard deviation: lognormal(log(1.5 s), 0.5), with the mean s of the standard deviations within the doses (of log(y) for lognormal), i.e. log(1/sigma^2) normal with mean -2 log(1.5 s) and standard deviation 1.

For the lognormal family, the priors of the background and the maximum response are priors of the median, exp(b1) or exp(b2). Informative priors are given as c(min, mode, max) (mode NA for the middle of the range) or as a prior, e.g. from fitpert.

The data need a control group at dose zero and at least two other doses, replicates at the doses (for the prior of the residual standard deviation), a positive response for the continuous families, and, for quantal responses, cbind(affected, unaffected) increasing with the dose.

References

EFSA Scientific Committee (2022). Guidance on the use of the benchmark dose approach in risk assessment. EFSA Journal 20(10), 7584.

Kremer, C., Saenen, N. D., Bijnens, K., Faes, C., De Boever, P., Smeets, K. and Aerts, M. (2026). Compilation of NTP and published dose-response data: study of informative priors in the EFSA platform for Bayesian benchmark dose analysis. EFSA Supporting Publications, EN-9902.

See also

bmdefsa, bmdbayes, fitpert, priors

Examples

# default priors of EFSA (2022) for the log-logistic model of the ryegrass data
efsapriors(rootl ~ conc, data = ryegrass, model = "loglogistic", family = "gaussian")
#> EFSA priors for the loglogistic model, gaussian family, decreasing curve, levelling off
#> BMD: relative, bmr = 0.05
#> 
#>   b1 ~ pert(0.151667, 0.303333, 7.28438)
#>   b2 ~ pert(3.87467, 7.74935, 15.4987)
#>   b3 ~ negate(lognormal(1, 1))
#>   bmd ~ pert(0, 15, 90, shape=0.0001)
#>   sigma ~ lognormal(-0.374202, 0.5)
# an informative prior of the BMD, by its minimum, mode and maximum
efsapriors(rootl ~ conc, data = ryegrass, model = "loglogistic", family = "gaussian",
           bmd = c(0.1, 1, 5))
#> EFSA priors for the loglogistic model, gaussian family, decreasing curve, levelling off
#> BMD: relative, bmr = 0.05
#> 
#>   b1 ~ pert(0.151667, 0.303333, 7.28438)
#>   b2 ~ pert(3.87467, 7.74935, 15.4987)
#>   b3 ~ negate(lognormal(1, 1))
#>   bmd ~ pert(0.1, 1, 5, shape=0.0001)
#>   sigma ~ lognormal(-0.374202, 0.5)
# the model with these priors, in the BMD parameterisation
e <- efsapriors(rootl ~ conc, data = ryegrass, model = "loglogistic", family = "gaussian")
fit <- drmTMB(rootl ~ conc, data = ryegrass, model = e$model, family = e$family,
              curvelink = e$curvelink, start = e$start, fix = e$fix, prior = e$prior,
              bmdpar = e$bmdpar)
summary(fit)
#> Call:
#> drmTMB(form = rootl ~ conc, data = ryegrass, start = e$start, 
#>     fix = e$fix, family = e$family, model = e$model, curvelink = e$curvelink, 
#>     prior = e$prior, bmdpar = e$bmdpar)
#> 
#> Model:  loglogistic, decreasing curve
#> Family: gaussian, identity link for the asymptotes
#> 
#> Number of observations: 24
#> Log-likelihood: -16.18 (df = 5), AIC: 42.36, BIC: 48.25
#> 
#> Priors:
#>   b1 ~ pert(0.151667, 0.303333, 7.28438)
#>   b2 ~ pert(3.87467, 7.74935, 15.4987)
#>   b3 ~ negate(lognormal(1, 1))
#>   bmd ~ pert(0, 15, 90, shape=0.0001)
#>   sigma ~ lognormal(-0.374202, 0.5)
#> 
#> Coefficients (posterior modes):
#>                Estimate Std. Error
#> b1:(Intercept)   0.4648      0.196
#> b2:(Intercept)   7.7913      0.176
#> b3:(Intercept)  -2.9634      0.425
#> log_bmd          0.1506      0.151
#> log_bmd is the log benchmark dose (relative, bmr = 0.05, decreasing curve) of the curve of the intercepts: BMD = 1.163
#> Fixed: b5:(Intercept) = 0
#> 
#> Residual standard deviation: 0.4886
#> 
#> Optimiser: nlminb: relative convergence (4), maximum absolute gradient 7.2e-10
